datasource_item.source_question_text:
A Chinook salmon can jump out of water with a speed v0 and an angle 𝜃 above the horizontal. What is the speed of the fish when it is at the maximum height?
A. 𝑣0. [incorrect]
B. 𝑣0 cos𝜃. [correct]
C. 𝑣0 sin𝜃. [incorrect]
D. 0. [incorrect]
datasource_item.generated_question_text:
A water droplet is launched from a fountain nozzle with speed v0 at an angle θ above the horizontal. What is the speed of the droplet when it reaches its maximum height (ignore air resistance)?
A. v0. [incorrect] Explanation: This is incorrect because the vertical component decreases to zero, so the total speed is less
than v0 (unless θ = 0).
B. v0 cos θ. [correct] Explanation: This is correct because at maximum height the vertical velocity is zero and the horizontal
component remains v0 cos θ.
C. v0 sin θ. [incorrect] Explanation: This is incorrect because v0 sin θ is the initial vertical component, which becomes zero at the
top.
D. 0. [incorrect] Explanation: This is incorrect because the droplet still has horizontal velocity at the top unless launched
straight up.

Which of the following statements is correct?
A. We can assume a "spherical cow" when analyzing the motion of a cow's leg. [incorrect]
B. We can safely assume a cow is a point mass when analyzing its position change in the scale of a mile over a certain time period. [correct]
C. We can never assume the cow is in a vacuum, even when we need to ignore the effect of air resistance. [incorrect]
D. None of the above is correct. [incorrect]

A. We can assume a “perfect sphere” model when analyzing the bending motion of a gymnast’s wrist. [incorrect] Explanation: This is incorrect because detailed limb motion depends on shape and joint geometry, so a spherical approximation is not appropriate.
B. We can reasonably treat a parade float as a point mass when estimating how far it travels over several kilometers in a given time. [correct] Explanation: Over kilometer-scale motion, the object’s size is negligible compared with its displacement, so a point-mass model is appropriate.
C. We are never allowed to model motion as if it occurred in a vacuum when we want to neglect air resistance. [incorrect] Explanation: This is incorrect because “vacuum” is a standard idealization used precisely to ignore drag effects when they are small.
D. None of the above is correct. [incorrect] Explanation: This is incorrect because option B describes a valid and commonly used approximation.
